newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller says stopped using Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller says stopped using Swiss banks.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller as of January 30 stopped the state from using Swiss banks for overnight investments until investigations into how Holocaust victims were treated are over, a spokeswoman said Thursday.
"The comptroller instructed his staff to use other banks until the review was completed," said Cynthia Monk, a spokeswoman for H. Carl McCall.
Monk said it was premature to speculate about what other options the state might take against the Swiss banks.
"At this point, we're reviewing our options," she said, adding McCall plans to speak at a February 13 hearing in New York City that will be held by Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan).
"We will develop a comprehensive plan," she added.

McCall is the trustee of the state's approximately $80 billion pension fund, which owns about $10.9 million of at least three Swiss banks, the spokeswoman said. The three banks are: Credit Suisse Group, Swiss Bank and the Union Bank of Switzerland.

Further, Brinson Partners, which the state has used to help manage its pension funds since the early 1990s and which was purchased by Swiss Bank, handles about $350 million for New York State's common retirement fund, she said.

New York State and New York City are the first state and local governments to get involved in the controversy over how Swiss banks treated Holocaust victims. New York State Governor George Pataki is sending the state banking superintendent to Switzerland to probe the activities of two banks, Swiss Bank and Credit Suisse, in World War Two.

And the New York City Council, which has drafted a bill that would stop the city from using Swiss banks for short-term investments, also said it would weigh having its pension fund sell Swiss bank stocks if the talks between the banks and Jewish Holocaust victims are not satisfactorily resolved.
